summary: Source update (read_only.go advance frees released ReadIndex requests) required a model change; reference, MC, Trace and Update suites were updated with three implementation-backed repairs, the prior harness was rebased and six fresh traces validated. Model checking found one real defect (MC-1): a reused read context can be released by an acknowledgement produced for its earlier request, yielding a stale ReadIndex; reproduced on the update revision, absent on the baseline.
validation_limits: All BFS/simulation campaigns except MC.cfg and MC_complete_core.cfg stopped at their time budgets (LIMITED_COVERAGE); none is an exhaustive proof.

The inherited MCView excludes fault counters, so even exhausted BFS runs merge states that differ only in remaining fault budget; full-reference admission of focused counterexamples was checked separately (spec/admit/).
Bounded model: 3 servers, 1-2 read contexts, MaxTerm <= 2, MaxLogLen <= 3, counter-bounded faults; snapshots, membership change, PreVote, leader transfer and lease reads remain out of scope.
Fresh traces cover 6 scenarios in a 3-server cluster; captured acknowledgement sets are always empty at observation points (first peer ack completes quorum).
No specula CLI or persistent-findings store is installed; ci-result generation and registry lookup could not be run (prior suite had no findings).

findings.title: Reused ReadIndex context released by an acknowledgement produced for the earlier request
findings.cause: readOnly.advance now frees released requests, so addRequest re-registers a context released earlier in the same leader term, while recvAck matches heartbeat responses only by context; a delayed response produced for the earlier registration completes the new one.
findings.trigger: Release ctx with one follower's ack while another follower's ack for ctx is delayed; a newer-term leader commits while the old leader is partitioned; the old leader registers ctx again and then receives the delayed ack.
findings.consequence: The old leader returns a ReadState whose index is lower than an entry committed before the read was issued (stale linearizable read, violating node.go:155-157).

premises: The application may reuse a ReadIndex request context after the previous request with that context completed (read_only.go:19-23 leaves the context to the caller).
Heartbeat responses can be delayed past a re-registration; the old leader has not yet stepped down (CheckQuorum is optional).
